<!-- pr-reviewer: 48354f313e78a16f8f7428f30c17ae409ec4814b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

**What looks good**
- Null id: a request with `"id": null` is answered -32600 with `id: null`. JSON-RPC 2.0 says the response id is null when the id could not be determined, so that is correct. A notification has no `id` key at all and stays silent (`id == Some(Null)` is distinct from `None`). MCP forbids null ids, so the refusal is right.
- `serve()` cap arithmetic is safe: `take(MAX+1)` with `try_from`/`saturating_add`. A line of exactly 16 MiB plus its newline is accepted. A longer one is detected as no trailing newline and `len > MAX`, then `skip_line` consumes `fill_buf` chunks until the newline, keeping nothing. Memory stays bounded at about 16 MiB. A cap-sized final line at EOF without a newline is still handled. `b'\n'` and `b"\n"` literals are correct.
- Non-UTF-8 lines give a -32700 parse error and the loop reads on. Only stream I/O errors end the loop.
- `lost()` checks arrays and leaves as present-leaf, recurses into objects, treats null as removal (RFC 7386), and handles an object patch that came back as a scalar. I found no `skip_serializing_if` on params types, so legitimate optional fields should not be falsely refused.
- No unwrap/expect/panic in the new code. `edit.rs` is 262 lines, `mod.rs` 234, `tools.rs` 230, all under 400. The module headers already carry provenance. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #443`, and no CHANGELOG.md edit.

**Local results (merged with current origin/main, clean automatic merge)**
| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp` | 8/8 pass (including the 4 new tests) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` | 95/95 pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `post` now reports `out["path"]` with a fallback to the requested path. It has no dedicated assertion, as the PR body says.
- Fork PRs #421, #422 and #428 also touch `mcp/mod.rs` and `tools.rs`. Whichever lands second takes a normal textual merge.
- The oversize test allocates about 16 MiB, which is fine.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
